subject: Geography
description: Highest peaks, longest ranges, fold vs block, Andes, Rockies, Alps, Himalayas

questions.stem: The world's HIGHEST peak (8,848.86 m) and its location:

options.option_text: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha / Chomolungma) — Mahalangur Himal of the Himalayas, Nepal-China (Tibet) border

questions.explanation: Mount Everest — height 8,848.86 m (revised from 8,848 m by joint Nepal-China survey, December 2020). Border peak — Sagarmatha (Nepali, head in the sky) / Chomolungma (Tibetan, mother goddess). Named after Sir George Everest (Surveyor General of India 1830-43). First confirmed summit — Edmund Hillary + Tenzing Norgay, 29 May 1953. K2 (Karakoram, Pakistan-China) — 8,611 m, 2nd highest, technically harder. Kanchenjunga — 8,586 m, India's HIGHEST peak (Sikkim-Nepal). Mont Blanc — Alps, only 4,807 m. 14 peaks > 8,000 m globally — all in Himalaya-Karakoram.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The LONGEST mountain range above sea level (~7,000 km along S America's western edge) is the:

options.option_text: Andes — runs through 7 countries (Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, Argentina)

questions.explanation: Andes — longest continental range, ~7,000 km, S American Pacific coast. Highest peak — Aconcagua (Argentina, 6,961 m, highest outside Asia + tallest in Western Hemisphere). Born from convergence of Nazca + South American plates. Many active volcanoes (Cotopaxi, Chimborazo, Llaullaillaco). Longest UNDERWATER mountain range — the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (~16,000 km, mostly submerged). Rockies — ~4,800 km, N America. Himalayas — ~2,400 km only. Tallest mountain measured base-to-summit — Mauna Kea (Hawaii, 10,200 m from ocean floor).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Himalayas are an example of:

options.option_text: Fold mountains (formed by collision of Indian + Eurasian plates ~50 Ma)

questions.explanation: Fold mountains — sedimentary layers on the seabed get crumpled when continental plates collide. Indian plate began separating from Africa-Antarctica ~150 Ma, drifted north at ~15 cm/yr. Collided with Eurasian plate ~50 Ma — Tethys Sea closed; sediments piled up to form Himalayas. Still rising ~5 mm/year! Other fold mtns: Andes, Alps, Atlas, Urals, Rockies. BLOCK mountains — rift / horst-graben (Vosges, Rhine valley). VOLCANIC — Mount Fuji, Vesuvius, Kilimanjaro. RESIDUAL — Aravallis (oldest fold mtn, now eroded to remnants). DOME — Black Hills (Dakota).

questions.stem: The HIGHEST mountain in Africa, also a free-standing volcano:

options.option_text: Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 m, in Tanzania) — dormant volcano

questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro — Tanzania, 5,895 m. Stratovolcano with three cones (Kibo, Mawenzi, Shira). Largest free-standing mountain (rises ~5 km from surrounding plain). Snow-capped summit (the icecap is shrinking due to climate change — could disappear by 2040). Mount Kenya — 2nd highest in Africa, 5,199 m. Other notable peaks: Mt Damavand (Iran, 5,610 m, highest in Middle East); Vinson Massif (Antarctica, 4,892 m); Mt Kosciuszko (Australia, 2,228 m, highest in Australia mainland; 'Seven Summits' challenge sometimes uses Mt Carstensz Pyramid in Indonesia at 4,884 m as the Oceania peak).

questions.stem: K2 (the world's 2nd highest peak) is in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: K2 (Mt Godwin-Austen / Chhogori) — 8,611 m, in the Karakoram range. India claims it as part of its territory (Pak-occupied Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan). 'K2' from the British Survey of India numbering — K1 = Masherbrum, K3 = Broad Peak. First summited 1954 (Italian expedition Lacedelli + Compagnoni). One of the deadliest 8000ers — climber fatality rate ~25%. Karakoram = 4 of the 14 eight-thousanders (K2, Gasherbrum I, II, Broad Peak). Plus Nanga Parbat (Himalaya, Gilgit-Baltistan), Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, Makalu, Annapurna … all 14 are in Pakistan, India, Nepal, China, with 8 in Nepal.

questions.stem: The Aravalli range — running ~700 km from Gujarat through Rajasthan to Delhi — is famous as:

options.option_text: One of the oldest fold mountain ranges on Earth (~3.5 billion years)

questions.explanation: Aravallis — formed in the Proterozoic (~3.5 Ga, earlier estimates 700 Ma), ancient Precambrian fold mountains. Have eroded substantially — current highest peak Guru Shikhar (Mt Abu, 1,722 m). Function as a critical biogeographic barrier — separating Thar Desert from Gangetic plains. Acts as 'green wall' protecting NCR. Mining + sand quarrying in Rajasthan — major environmental damage; SC banned mining in protected stretches. Compare Western Ghats (~150 Ma, much younger), Eastern Ghats (similar age to Aravallis but different orogeny), Himalayas (~50 Ma, youngest).

questions.stem: Match peak with continent — INCORRECT pairing:
questions.explanation: Vinson Massif (4,892 m) is in ANTARCTICA (Ellsworth Mountains) — not Africa. Africa's highest is Kilimanjaro. The 'Seven Summits' (highest peak on each continent): Asia — Everest (8,849); S America — Aconcagua (6,961); N America — Denali (6,190; renamed back from McKinley in 2025); Africa — Kilimanjaro (5,895); Europe — Elbrus (5,642, Russia); Antarctica — Vinson Massif (4,892); Oceania — Carstensz Pyramid (4,884) or Kosciuszko (2,228, Aus mainland) — debated. Reinhold Messner's list uses Carstensz; original Bass list uses Kosciuszko.
